personality_one_liner: A friendly, touchable, and vibrant shared space that makes group coordination feel like a breeze rather than a chore.

spacing.rule: Generous padding around chunky cards, controlled asymmetry, and grouped modular layouts instead of flat lists.

do's: Use glass on the bottom tab bar when content scrolls behind it.
Use glass on sticky headers (e.g., month/week toggle headers) over scrolling calendars.
dont's: Never apply glass to the calendar blocks, buttons, list rows, or standard cards.

screens.name: Login & Auth
screens.purpose: A playful entry point for signing up, joining a group via invite code, or logging in.

states.error: Inline form errors with red highlights and shake animation.

screens.layout: Bottom-heavy layout with sticky primary CTA. Inputs have pill shapes and sit on a clean surface.

screens.name: Mój plan (My Plan)
screens.purpose: Personal calendar to view and add one-time or recurring plans.

states.empty: Warm illustration of a notebook with a 'Add your first plan' CTA.
states.error: Card with readable error and retry button.

screens.layout: Segmented control at the top (Month/Week). Week view uses a horizontal scroll carousel for dates and vertical for time. Use a bottom sheet for the 'Add Plan' action to keep users in context.

screens.name: Ludzie (Users)
screens.purpose: List of group members where clicking one shows their personal plan.

states.loading: List of skeleton avatars and names.
states.empty: Illustration of friends with a 'Share invite code' CTA.

screens.layout: Grid or stacked cards of users with large avatars. Tapping a user opens their calendar via a bottom sheet or a detail page.

screens.name: Wspólny (Shared Calendar)
screens.purpose: The ultimate overlaid calendar where everyone's plans are visible in unique colors.

states.loading: Skeleton of grid with faded colored blocks.
states.error: Error banner over the calendar grid.

screens.layout: Sticky glass header for date selection. A dense but smooth FlatList/ScrollView (60fps optimized) grid where users' plans are rendered as rounded, uniquely colored (using userColors) overlapping blocks.

screens.name: Wolne (Free Days)
screens.purpose: A curated list of entirely free days calculated by the app.

states.empty: Illustration of a busy schedule with 'No free days this month!' text.

screens.layout: Vertical list of chunky, celebratory cards for each free day. Each card has a primary CTA 'Propose Meeting' that opens a bottom sheet.

screens.name: Spotkania (Meetings)
screens.purpose: A hub for proposed meetings where users can RSVP and discuss details.

states.empty: Empty state illustration of a coffee cup with 'No upcoming meetings.'

screens.layout: Feed of meeting cards. Cards include a title, date/time, place, notes, and clear pill-shaped 'Going' / 'Not Going' RSVP buttons. Tapping the card opens a detail sheet.

empty_state_friends.alt: Group of friends laughing and high-fiving

empty_state_planner.alt: Open monthly planner on a wooden desk

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the 'Tactile / Playful' layout: use chunky cards, generous padding, pill-shaped buttons, and rounded corners to make the app approachable.
Use @gorhom/bottom-sheet for core actions like 'Add Plan', 'View Member Calendar', and 'Propose Meeting'. This keeps the user within the main context.

For the Shared Calendar (Wspólny), ensure performance is 60fps by utilizing FlatList/virtualization. Render individual user plans as distinct, colorful, rounded blocks using the custom non-blue 'userColors' array provided.
Implement a sticky segmented control for toggling between Month and Week views on the calendar screens.
Whenever displaying imagery with text overlaid, ALWAYS apply a top-to-bottom dark gradient scrim to guarantee text contrast.
All blue, purple, magenta, orange, and terracotta hues are strictly banned as primary or accent colors. Stick to the provided botanical and earthy yellows/greens.
Implement the sticky primary CTA over scrolling content pattern (with bottom safe-area clearance) on forms like 'Add Plan' or 'Create Meeting'.
